AI // ML

AI & Machine Learning in Cybersecurity

Where machine learning strengthens defense — detecting threats faster, cutting alert noise — and where AI systems themselves become the attack surface.

01 DATALogs, packets, endpoints, emails
02 FEATURESBehavior, frequency, entropy, context
03 MODELAnomaly detection & classifiers
04 ALERTRisk score + explainable signal
05 ANALYSTHuman triage & feedback loop
Detection

ANOMALY DETECTION

Unsupervised models learn what normal looks like on a network, then flag deviations such as unusual login times, data exfiltration spikes or lateral movement.

Isolation Forest · Autoencoders · Clustering
Malware

MALWARE CLASSIFICATION

Classifiers trained on static and behavioral features (API calls, opcodes, file entropy) separate benign from malicious samples and group new variants into families.

Random Forest · Gradient Boosting · Deep Learning
Email Security

PHISHING DETECTION

NLP models score message text, URLs and sender patterns to catch phishing and business-email-compromise that signature rules miss.

NLP · URL Features · Text Classification
Network

INTRUSION DETECTION

ML-assisted IDS profiles traffic flows to spot scans, C2 beaconing and DDoS patterns, complementing signature-based tools like Snort and Suricata.

NetFlow · CICIDS-style Datasets · Zeek
SOC

UEBA & ALERT TRIAGE

User and entity behavior analytics builds baselines per account, while ML-based prioritization reduces false positives so analysts focus on real incidents.

SIEM · Risk Scoring · Correlation
Automation

LLM-ASSISTED SECURITY

Language models help summarize incidents, explain logs, draft detection rules and speed up reporting — always with a human verifying the output.

Log Summarization · Report Drafting · Playbooks
anomaly_detector.py — concept demo
from sklearn.ensemble import IsolationForest
import pandas as pd

# flow features: bytes, packets, duration, dst_ports
df = pd.read_csv("network_flows.csv")

model = IsolationForest(contamination=0.01, random_state=42)
model.fit(df)

df["score"] = model.decision_function(df)
df["suspicious"] = model.predict(df) == -1

# send top outliers to an analyst for review
print(df[df.suspicious].nsmallest(10, "score"))

[!] SECURING AI SYSTEMS

  • Prompt InjectionMalicious input that hijacks an LLM's instructions.
  • Data PoisoningTampered training data that corrupts model behavior.
  • Adversarial EvasionCrafted inputs that slip past ML detectors.
  • Model Theft & LeakageExtraction of models or sensitive training data.
  • AI-Powered Social EngineeringDeepfakes and generated phishing at scale.
